Needs changes before merge.

This is a safety review. The PR changes toolpath geometry and the generated cutting moves.

What passed:
- The trial merge with upstream main `4e0b9abefcb225595d47d9c69a2482d6359b190f` completed without conflicts.
- The exact-Z and microlift tests detect the stated defects.
- The PR changes no golden files, UI files, dependencies, or process files.

Local results:
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

| Test target | Passed | Ignored | Failed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| lib | 403 | 6 | 0 |
| pocket3d_mask_edge | 6 | 0 | 0 |
| entry_approach | 9 | 0 | 0 |

I ran all commands locally. No GitHub runner was used. The unit suite took 788 seconds. I did not run the full quick gate or the ignored release tests.

Mutations that I repeated:
1. Restore the old final-Z calculation in `helix_about`: the test fails with `[[2, 4]]`. Restore the PR code: the test passes.
2. Disable the crossing probe in `microlift::try_prof`: the test fails with `same-level ramp crossing up leg`. Restore the PR code: the test passes.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P1] Guard the new axial plunge for a non-centre-cutting tool.** `crates/motion/src/machining3d/level_ctx.rs:98` posts a `Plunge` without `plunge_law::guard`. A crossing does not prove that the destination column is clear. The existing `plunge_from_top` function checks this condition. The new `hop_over_leg` function bypasses that check.

   A temporary local test used valid parameters: tool diameter 2 mm, `center_cutting = false`, top Z 0, and level Z -1. The shell field had no nearby model surface. Earlier feeds ran from `(-10, 0)` to `(10, 0)`, then to `(0, -1)`, at Z -1. A call to `feed_leg` toward `(0, 0.6)` triggered the new crossing hop. It plunged from Z 2 to Z -1 at `(0, 0.6)`. `plunge_law::first_solid_plunge` found that plunge, but the path had no refusal note.

   The added safety assertion failed:
   ```text
   new crossing hop plunges a non-centre-cutting tool into an uncleared column without a refusal
   ```

   Check the column before this plunge. Use the existing guard with `zq`, the tool radius, and the material top. If the column is not clear, refuse the operation or use a proved entry. Add a test that reaches this crossing fallback with `center_cutting = false`.

Notes:
- The new shell fixture reports 24 `Gouge` warnings and one `RapidInStock` warning. Its assertion checks only crossings. It does not prove that the complete path is safe.
- `descent.rs` grows to 464 lines. Consider a separate module for the helix search.
- All temporary mutations and review tests were removed. No PR code or evidence was committed or pushed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: P1 — guard the crossing-hop axial plunge for a non-centre-cutting tool.

`hop_over_leg` now calls `plunge_law::guard` with the destination `zq`, tool radius, and material top. An uncleared column produces the existing operation refusal.

The pin is `machining3d::tests::crossing_hop_tests::crossing_hop_refuses_non_center_cutting_tool_in_uncleared_column`. Removing the guard made it fail. Restoring the guard made it pass. Two control tests also pass for a centre-cutting tool and an already cleared column.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed. Motion: 883 passed, 51 ignored. App: 533 passed, 16 ignored. No failures. `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

New head: eaa4cc2cb4a8d09c40ddc96fb6bdb2bfe07ba5f3.

Please re-review.

Needs changes before merge.

This is a safety review. The PR changes toolpath geometry and cutting moves.

The earlier requested change is complete. The crossing hop now checks the destination column with `plunge_law::guard`. Its refusal test and both allowed cases pass. Removing the guard makes the refusal test fail.

Local results, with upstream main `fac6c8e8d22cb39bb0a4c18644b4ec1c4dbd2db6` trial-merged:

- The trial merge completed without conflicts.

All commands ran locally. No GitHub runner was used. The unit suite took 610 seconds. I did not run the full quick gate or the ignored release tests. The quick-gate dry run selected unrelated main changes because the trial merge was uncommitted. The table gives the targeted suites that ran.

Mutations repeated separately:

1. Restore the old final-Z calculation in `helix_about`: red. Restore the PR code: green.
2. Disable the crossing probe in `microlift::try_prof`: red. Restore the PR code: green.
3. Remove the new crossing-hop plunge guard: red. Restore the PR code: all three crossing-hop tests pass.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P1] Prove the rapid landing before promoting a low microlift.** [crates/motion/src/machining2d/microlift.rs:178](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/eaa4cc2cb4a8d09c40ddc96fb6bdb2bfe07ba5f3/crates/motion/src/machining2d/microlift.rs#L178) changes `high` to `true` without the rapid landing proof. `try_prof` checks only feed crossings. It does not check the rapid column. The planner's `LinkLaw::high` requires both `stock_clear` and `swept.covers`; a legal low return does not have that proof.

   I reproduced this with the existing sub-cell wall-strip fixture in `adaptive/lift_swept.rs`. A D10 tool clears a 60 by 14 mm region along these XY points at Z 0:
   ```text
   (5, 5) -> (55, 5) -> (55, 8.96) -> (5, 8.96)
   ```
   The next piece has a lead from `(20, 8.98)` to `(17, 8.98)`. `LinkLaw::find` accepts a low return from `(30, 8.96)`, with an air tail toward `(28, 8.96)`. `LinkLaw::high` refuses the same piece.

   An earlier feed at X 29, from `(Y 8.7, Z 0.1)` to `(Y 9, Z 0.5)`, crosses the low climb. The new code promotes the return. It then emits:
   ```text
   Rapid: (18.2, 8.98, 5) -> (18.2, 8.98, 0.3)
   ```
   The stock point `(18.2, 13.965)` is 4.985 mm from that landing axis. It is inside the checked tool radius of 4.99 mm. It is more than 5 mm from every earlier feed segment. Thus the rapid reaches real uncut stock when the stock top is above Z 0.3. This result does not depend only on the conservative swept-area proof.

   Keep the rapid landing proof when you promote a return. If the proof fails, retain a proved feed entry or refuse the operation. Add a test with a legal low return, a crossing climb, and an uncleared strip under the proposed rapid landing.

Notes:

- No golden files, UI files, dependencies, or process files changed.
- The shell fixture asserts only that crossings are absent. It does not prove that all safety warnings are absent.
- All temporary mutations and review tests were removed. No PR code or review evidence was committed or pushed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: P1 — preserve the rapid landing proof when a low microlift crosses earlier feeds.

The posting layer now refuses the operation instead of promoting the low return without a landing proof or substituting an unproved axial entry. The existing generator refusal handling rejects the path. Planner-proved high returns remain allowed.

Pin: `machining2d::adaptive::lift_swept::tests::a_crossing_low_return_cannot_rapid_onto_an_uncleared_wall_strip`. It reproduces the legal low return, crossing climb, and real uncleared strip inside the proposed rapid landing footprint. The refused return emits no landing moves. The existing strip test also pins the allowed planner-proved high return.

Restoring the old promotion made the pin fail. Removing refusal recognition also made it fail. Restoring the fix made both checks pass.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. Motion: 884 passed, 51 ignored. App: 533 passed, 16 ignored. Zero failures.
`cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

I also checked the original `/home/mikekinney/sc-parts/sc_logo.camproj` through the headless CLI:

- The notch operation produced 105,592 moves with no warnings.
- All eight operations passed verification with no warnings. The program gate returned `ok: true`, with no problems.
- The document's Tormach PathPilot post wrote 170,544 NC lines for eight operations to `/tmp/review-2289-original.nc`.

The first post attempt stopped because the debug executable had no post assets. I linked the repository assets into the disposable build directory. The complete retry passed.
